title: PSA finds evidence of Joseph Sy's 'fake' records
summary: The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) said Thursday it found evidence showing that embattled businessman Joseph Sy procured fake documents during his birth registration process.

blocks.text: The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) said Thursday it found evidence showing that embattled businessman Joseph Sy procured fake documents during his birth registration process.

PSA Legal Service Director Atty. Eliezer Ambatali said this during the continuation of the Senate Committee on Justice and Human Rights’ hearing into the case of Sy---a nickel businessman who was previously arrested after his biometrics matched those of a Chinese citizen Chen Zhong Zhen.
Ambatali said the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) has already filed a petition for the cancellation of the birth records of Sy.

“Doon sa investigation namin…investigation ng Fraud Management Division ito ng PSA, we found out that there is evidence that would say na merong…mga procurement ng fake documents during the registration,” Ambatali said.
(In our investigation, conducted by the PSA’s Fraud Management Division, we discovered evidence indicating that fake documents were procured during Sy’s registration process.)

“This type of fraud is the second type. It happens at the source, during the registration. So these are fake ‘yung baptismal certificate…hindi makita ‘yung birth records ng mga magulang, hindi rin namin makita ‘yung mga records ng hilot or ‘yung attending person during the time of birth,” he added.

(This type of fraud is the second type. It happens at the source, during the registration. For instance, we found that his baptismal certificates are fake; we cannot locate his parents’ birth records nor any records from his birth attendant or the person who assisted during his birth.)
Suspected of being a Chinese national parading as a Filipino, Sy was arrested by Philippine authorities in 2025 when he arrived at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport from Hong Kong.
But the Supreme Court (SC) First Division ordered last month the release of Sy, ruling in favor of his petition for habeas corpus.
The Bureau of Immigration (BI) said it respected the SC’s resolution on the petition, but clarified that the Court did not settle the matter of Sy’s nationality.
Fingerprints
Meanwhile, Bureau of Immigration (BI) Deputy Commissioner Atty. Joel Alejandro Nacnac also confirmed during the hearing that the fingerprints of Sy matched those of Chinese national Chen Zhong Zhen.
Committee chairperson Sen. Risa Hontiveros then asked when the fingerprints of Sy entered the BI database.
“Under our records, he is an applicant po ng returning resident visa way back in 1989. Subsequently, the permanent resident visa was approved in February of 1989,” Nacnac said.

“Later on, he also applied under RA 7919, it po ‘yung Alien Social Integration Program, which appears to be on record, March of 1996 na po. With this, ‘yung biometric records niya ay nakita at na-capture po ng Bureau,” he added.
(Later on, he also applied for the Alien Social Integration Program, which appears to be on record, March of 1996. With this, his biometric records were seen and captured by the Bureau.)
No show
Sy, who is the subject of the investigation, also failed to attend the hearing.
His lawyer, Alma Mallonga, said that the businessman called earlier this morning to say that he was in an emergency room of Makati Medical Center and “had been feeling unwell since last night.”

“Maybe part of it is the stress. The fact that he had been incarcerated for more than 491 days, Your Honor, and it’s just been less than three weeks since he was released,” Mallonga said, adding that her client also underwent certain “surgical procedures.”
Regardless, the lawyer said Sy had earlier expressed intent to attend the hearing.

Hontiveros, on the other hand, asked Sy’s lawyer to submit a medical certificate and instructed the committee secretary to coordinate with the Senate clinic to validate the condition of the embattled businessman.
The senator also said she is expecting that Sy will be attending the next committee hearing.
“Mr. Joseph Sy, inaasahan kita sa susunod na hearing. Kung kaya mo mag party-party, Baka kaya mo ring dumalo at harapin ang Senado ng Pilipinas,” Hontiveros said.
(Mr. Joseph Sy, I expect to see you at the next hearing. If you’re capable of partying, perhaps you’re also capable of attending and facing the Philippine Senate.) —LDF, GMA News
